reasoning_traces.think:
The audit exposes a fundamental duality between structural existence and semantic validity within a retrieval corpus. Initially, the system operated under a flawed assumption that file presence on disk equated to indexable knowledge. This led to a singularity where 37 byte-identical duplicates and a single truncated download created redundant topological nodes, while high-value `.md` files were effectively erased by 0-character `openalex` stubs. Mathematically, this is a failure of the ranking operator $R(d)$ to account for the information entropy $H(d)$ of the payload. The introduction of the `has_full_text` flag acts as a hard constraint, redefining the search space such that $\forall d_{stub}, d_{full}$, if $Title(d_{stub}) = Title(d_{full})$, then $Rank(d_{full}) > Rank(d_{stub})$. Furthermore, the `query_domain` bug illustrates a severe leakage in the feature extraction manifold. By defaulting all non-soccer queries to `american_football`, the system forced orthogonal vector spaces (like cybersecurity) into a highly constrained tactical subspace. This caused high-BM25 matches to be artificially penalized during the cross-encoder fusion phase. The resolution required expanding the lexical basis vectors (`_AF_TOKENS`) and implementing a rigorous zero-signal fallback (`OTHER_DOMAIN`). This dual correction—prioritizing empirical payload over metadata priors, and enforcing strict domain orthogonality—restores the mathematical integrity of the retrieval graph, ensuring that the fused relevance score accurately reflects the underlying geometric proximity between query intent and document reality.
